newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECHS ANNOUNCE MIN BID FOR AERO STAKE.
newsitem.headline: CZECHS ANNOUNCE MIN BID FOR AERO STAKE.

text.p: Bidders in a tender for a 34 to 40 percent stake in Czech aircraft maker Aero Vodochody a.s. must offer a mimimum of 950 million crowns for the shares, Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Thursday.
He told a news conference that the tender, open to domestic and foreign concerns seeking to revitalise the troubled jet aircraft firm, would be officially opened around January 20.
As categories of criteria for the tender, Dlouhy said a commission to evaluate bids would measure the bidders' economic strength, obligations to other shareholders and their strategic position.
Dlouhy said state-controlled Aero shareholders would pass their shareholders' rights to the new investor in order to allow him to manage the company from a majority position.
The cabinet approved the tender rules on Wednesday, and Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said the winner would be known in April.
Dlouhy noted that strategic considerations might convince the steering committee to pick a Czech domestic partner for Aero.

"If, for example, the Defence Ministry submits such arguents which will persuade the commission that it is necessary... to prefer a domestic investor, it will be a criterium well defined and followed by the commission.
"But we do not want to consider it open only for domestic companies from the beginning," he said.

The Czech chemical and arms conglomerate Chemapol Group a.s. has shown an interest in Aero, as well as local trading company CIMEX Holding a.s., and U.S. Boeing Co in an alliance with Czech air carrier Ceske Aerolinie a.s..
State-controlled shareholders of the debt-strapped company approved a cut in Aero's basic capital last month to one million crowns from 962 million, in a financial restructuring plan.
They also agreed to subsequently underwrite a rights issue to raise equity to between 1.74 and 2.5 billion crowns as a part of the deal.
